record.original_question: For the Recamán sequence defined by a_0=0 and a_n=a_{n-1}-n when that value is positive and has not appeared earlier, and a_n=a_{n-1}+n otherwise, remove repeated values and form the associated 4-regular graphs of initial segments. Give a precise explanation of the extraordinary graph structure that appears after duplicates are removed.

evidence.quote: The Recaman sequence (A005132), first defined by Bernardo Recaman Santos in a letter to N. J. A. Sloane in 1991, is a well-known sequence. It is given by a_0 = 0 and a_n = a_{n-1} - n if a_{n-1} > n and not already in the sequence, and a_n = a_{n-1} + n otherwise.

Graphing the sequences after removing all duplicates results in a quite interesting graph. It is difficult to make a very precise statement but the graph immediately shows the presence of extraordinary structure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the Recamán sequence $(a_n)_{n\ge 0}$ by $a_0 = 0$ and, for $n \ge 1$,
\[ a_n = \begin{cases} a_{n-1} - n & \text{if } a_{n-1} - n > 0 \text{ and } a_{n-1}-n \notin \{a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{n-1}\}, \\ a_{n-1} + n & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]
For each $N \ge 1$, let $S_N$ be the multiset $\{a_0,a_1,\dots,a_N\}$ and let $T_N \subseteq S_N$ be the set obtained by deleting every element of $S_N$ that occurs more than once (i.e., keeping only those values that appear exactly once in the segment). Re-index the retained values in their original order of appearance as $b_0,b_1,\dots,b_{M(N)}$, and form the 4-regular circulant-like graph $G_N$ on vertex set $\{0,1,\dots,M(N)\}$ in which each index $i$ is joined to $i\pm 1$ and $i\pm 2$ (mod $M(N)+1$), with the vertex $i$ embedded in the plane at the point $(i, b_i)$.

Give a precise mathematical description of the large-scale structure exhibited by the family of graphs $\{G_N\}_{N\to\infty}$ (for instance, asymptotic density of retained terms, the distribution of gaps $b_{i+1}-b_i$, recurring geometric patterns of the planar embedding, or any provable self-similarity), formulated as a rigorous statement and proof.
artifact.status_search_result: The Recamán sequence (OEIS A005132) is well known and has many empirical observations, but no rigorous theorem characterizing the "extraordinary structure" of graphs obtained from initial segments after removing duplicate values appears in the literature. Even basic conjectures about A005132 (e.g., whether every nonnegative integer eventually appears) remain open, so the more refined structural question is also open.

status_evidence.title: OEIS A005132 — Recamán's sequence
status_evidence.snippet: It is conjectured that every number eventually appears... still open as of recent updates.
status_evidence.claim: Basic structural questions about the Recamán sequence remain unresolved.
